title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles became unable to complete their routes when their batteries depleted during unexpected heavy traffic on Fourth of July. The system was deployed in conditions it was not built to handle: major unplanned road closures and traffic volumes that exceeded design assumptions. Better traffic prediction, higher battery capacity for peak demand scenarios, or human override protocols to redirect vehicles before battery depletion would have prevented stranding.

The incident shows a gap between testing conditions and real-world deployment. Autonomous vehicles were sent into service on a day with predictable but major traffic disruptions. One vehicle also caught fire after driving over fireworks, revealing exposure to hazards outside normal operating parameters. It is not established whether Waymo could have anticipated these specific conditions or whether other safeguards would have prevented the fire.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, many of them Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following fireworks displays. The company attributed the situation to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to tow the vehicles away. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported.

The incident has prompted discussions among city officials about improving traffic management for future events. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to hold conversations with public and private partners to ensure smoother outcomes next year. Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to strengthen its resilience during major traffic disruptions. This incident follows a December power outage that also left some Waymo vehicles stranded at non-functioning traffic lights in San Francisco.
